{"cells":[{"cell_type":"markdown","metadata":{},"source":"
Kaggriculture · public strategy experiment

Where the Wheat Remembers Tomorrow

A two-move market game hidden inside a 719-step farm—and a deliberately transparent attempt to turn a strong public trajectory into a broader, more balanced policy.

> **Version 2 · public evidence update.** The agent artifact is byte-for-byte unchanged. This revision adds an immutable 13-episode public snapshot and its exact completed submission row. "},{"cell_type":"markdown","metadata":{},"source":"## The idea Many strong public agents appear complicated because their farms are long. Yet one unusually consequential decision happens before the farm has really begun: how much wheat inventory to acquire, then immediately release while the rest of the opening is assembled. I started from a **publicly observable action trajectory** by LagrangianLocomotive, one of the leading teams at collection time. I did not access their private code. The downstream trajectory is preserved as public-behavior research; the opening is independently swept and changed from **buy 53 / sell 48** to **buy 45 / sell 40**. That distinction matters: this is an empirical route derivative, not a claim to have recovered another competitor's private strategy. It is published so the experiment can be inspected, reproduced, and improved. "},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":null,"metadata":{},"outputs":[],"source":"# Frozen local-screen evidence embedded for reproducibility. # 20 current top-10 public trajectories, all eight first-shop regimes, # 200 seeds per pairing and both seats = 1,216,000 simulated games. family_outcome = {'BAKERY': 0.725, 'BRUNCH_SPOT': 0.97375, 'FARMERS_MARKET': 0.824167, 'ICE_CREAM_SHOP': 0.9625, 'PET_CAFE': 0.83875, 'PIZZA_SHOP': 0.632083, 'SMOOTHIE_SHOP': 0.55375, 'YARN_STORE': 0.684318} summary = { "games": 1_216_000, "family_macro_outcome": 0.7742897727, "minimum_shop_family_outcome": 0.55375, "seat_0_outcome": 0.709375, "seat_1_outcome": 0.713875, "clipped_mean_margin": 5379.9542, "opening": "buy 45 wheat, sell 40 wheat", } print("Frozen local screen") for key, value in summary.items(): print(f"{key:>28}: {value}") "},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":null,"metadata":{},"outputs":[],"source":"import matplotlib.pyplot as plt labels = [name.replace("_", " ").title() for name in family_outcome] values = list(family_outcome.values()) colors = ["#b48a35" if value == min(values) else "#2f6b59" for value in values] fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.2)) bars = ax.barh(labels, values, color=colors) ax.axvline(0.5, color="#992f2f", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.2, label="even outcome") ax.set_xlim(0, 1) ax.set_xlabel("Local route-screen outcome (1 = win, 0.5 = draw)") ax.set_title("Q45 opening across every first-shop regime", loc="left", weight="bold") ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=.16) ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="lower right") for bar, value in zip(bars, values): ax.text(value + .012, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f"{value:.3f}", va="center") plt.tight_layout() plt.show() "},{"cell_type":"markdown","metadata":{},"source":"## What changed—and what did not The route screen found the same late structure repeatedly in competitive Yarn episodes: a modest early flock, then a much larger sheep-and-pasture economy. The best public trajectory in the first screen beat a broad historical panel, but its original 53-unit opening was brittle when challenged against leaders from **all** shop regimes. The quantity sweep exposed a useful counterfactual: | Opening | All-regime macro outcome | Weakest shop family | |---|---:|---:| | Original Q53 | 0.522 | 0.293 | | **Retuned Q45** | **0.774** | **0.554** | | Nearby Q50 | 0.759 | 0.551 | Only the first two market calls were altered. Everything after that stays fixed. This makes the hypothesis unusually clean: the opening inventory wedge changes which economy survives long enough for the late livestock plan to matter. The numbers above are from deterministic local C++ simulation panels. They are useful selection evidence, but they are **not** Kaggle public scores. A separate exact-engine campaign is still running before this idea is considered for the Moon/Soil line. "},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":null,"metadata":{},"outputs":[],"source":"# Materialize the exact, hash-pinned Python agent. import base64 import hashlib from pathlib import Path AGENT_B64 = '' EXPECTED_AGENT_SHA256 = "7aacd7233e5113e41024db0ff85912ab13cbd164e85ed5438af17df25a85b287" agent_bytes = base64.b64decode(AGENT_B64) actual_agent_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(agent_bytes).hexdigest() assert actual_agent_sha256 == EXPECTED_AGENT_SHA256 output_dir = Path("/kaggle/working") if Path("/kaggle/working").is_dir() else Path.cwd() / "notebook_output" output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) main_path = output_dir / "main.py" main_path.write_bytes(agent_bytes) print(f"main.py: {len(agent_bytes):,} bytes") print(f"sha256: {actual_agent_sha256}") "},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":null,"metadata":{},"outputs":[],"source":"# Structural checks: exact opening, legal response shape, both seats. namespace = {} exec(compile(agent_bytes, "main.py", "exec"), namespace) actions = namespace["_ACTIONS"] assert len(actions) == 719 assert actions[0]["market"] == [["BUY_PRODUCT", "WHEAT", 45]] assert actions[1]["market"][0] == ["SELL", "WHEAT", 40] mock_obs = {"step": 0, "player": 0, "farms": [{"hands": []}, {"hands": []}]} for seat in (0, 1): mock_obs["player"] = seat response = namespace["agent"](mock_obs, {}) assert set(response) == {"farmer", "hands", "market"} assert response["market"] == [["BUY_PRODUCT", "WHEAT", 45]] print("PASS: 719 actions, Q45/Q40 opening, valid response shape, both seats") "},{"cell_type":"code","execution_count":null,"metadata":{},"outputs":[],"source":"# Build a deterministic submission bundle containing exactly root-level main.py. import gzip import io import tarfile tar_buffer = io.BytesIO() with tarfile.open(fileobj=tar_buffer, mode="w") as bundle: info = tarfile.TarInfo("main.py") info.size = len(agent_bytes) info.mode = 0o644 info.mtime = 0 bundle.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(agent_bytes)) submission_bytes = gzip.compress(tar_buffer.getvalue(), compresslevel=9, mtime=0) submission_path = output_dir / "submission.tar.gz" submission_path.write_bytes(submission_bytes) with tarfile.open(submission_path, "r:gz") as bundle: members = bundle.getnames() extracted = bundle.extractfile("main.py").read() assert members == ["main.py"] assert extracted == agent_bytes print(f"submission.tar.gz: {len(submission_bytes):,} bytes") print(f"sha256: {hashlib.sha256(submission_bytes).hexdigest()}") print("members:", members) "},{"cell_type":"markdown","metadata":{},"source":"## The public ladder begins to answer The first completed Kaggle row now provides a real, if still early, external test. At the frozen snapshot below, Q45 had played **13 public episodes and won all 13**, reaching an exact completed-row score of **1887.4**. Opponents ranged from **574.0 to 1799.7** initial rating; the narrowest win was **+3,213**.

Top-10 cutoff
2833.8
That final comparison is essential. An unbeaten opening run is encouraging, but it is not evidence that the fixed route has reached top-ten strength. [{'episode': 1, 'opponent': 'Arunabh Gupta', 'opponent_initial_rating': 634.362, 'margin': 81807, 'rating': 719.151, 'seat': 0}, {'episode': 2, 'opponent': 'omarkami007', 'opponent_initial_rating': 574.007, 'margin': 92164, 'rating': 788.981, 'seat': 1}, {'episode': 3, 'opponent': 'jenninglim', 'opponent_initial_rating': 746.504, 'margin': 59375, 'rating': 885.543, 'seat': 1}, {'episode': 4, 'opponent': 'page0526', 'opponent_initial_rating': 813.91, 'margin': 56327, 'rating': 974.09, 'seat': 1}, {'episode': 5, 'opponent': 'RuiKimura4', 'opponent_initial_rating': 920.736, 'margin': 45139, 'rating': 1067.624, 'seat': 0}, {'episode': 6, 'opponent': 'Sakthei', 'opponent_initial_rating': 1098.627, 'margin': 24967, 'rating': 1185.473, 'seat': 0}, {'episode': 7, 'opponent': 'Darren Amadeus 1424.479, 'seat': 1}, {'episode': 9, 'opponent': 'MrAnalyst', 'opponent_initial_rating': 1267.742, 'margin': 8449, 'rating': 1491.153, 'seat': 0}, {'episode': 10, 'opponent': 'd0gied', 'opponent_initial_rating': 1439.372, 'margin': 3213, 'rating': 1585.122, 'seat': 0}, {'episode': 11, 'opponent': 'Zhizhou Sha', 'opponent_initial_rating': 1629.838, 'margin': 42688, 'rating': 1707.468, 'seat': 0}, {'episode': 12, 'opponent': 'K.nosaka', 'opponent_initial_rating': 1529.0, 'margin': 9910, 'rating': 1769.562, 'seat': 1}, {'episode': 13, 'opponent': 'Violet Notes', 'opponent_initial_rating': 1799.689, 'margin': 30328, 'rating': 1887.416, 'seat': 0}] official_public_score = 1887.4 top10_cutoff_at_snapshot = 2833.8 team_best_at_snapshot = 2208.8 import statistics import matplotlib.pyplot as plt opponent_rating = [row["opponent_initial_rating"] for row in public_episodes] margin = [row["margin"] for row in public_episodes] trajectory = [row["rating"] for row in public_episodes] strength_margin_correlation = statistics.correlation(opponent_rating, margin) fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.8)) left.plot(range(1, 14), trajectory, marker="o", color="#2f6b59", linewidth=2) left.axhline(top10_cutoff_at_snapshot, color="#992f2f", linestyle="--", label="top-10 cutoff") left.axhline(team_best_at_snapshot, color="#b48a35", linestyle=":", label="team best") left.set(title="Public rating trajectory", xlabel="Completed episode", ylabel="Rating") left.grid(alpha=.16) left.legend(frameon=False) right.scatter(opponent_rating, margin, c=range(1, 14), cmap="viridis", s=58) right.axhline(0, color="#992f2f", linestyle="--", linewidth=1) right.set(title="Margins narrow as opponents strengthen", xlabel="Opponent initial rating", ylabel="Winning margin") right.grid(alpha=.16) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() print(f"13–0 · official row {official_public_score:.1f} · strength/margin correlation {strength_margin_correlation:.3f}") "},{"cell_type":"markdown","metadata":{},"source":"### What the curve says The useful signal is not merely “13 wins.” As matchmaking strengthened, margins generally narrowed: the frozen opponent-strength/margin correlation is about **−0.746**. Q45 therefore looks like a sound fixed opening and a valuable control, while the remaining gap argues for a dynamic policy that responds to observable opponent behavior. The ongoing follow-up freezes exactly that question: whether call-1 market programs can be selected from shared state without relying on opponent identity. Until those exact tests finish, this notebook remains an experiment rather than a promotion claim. "},{"cell_type":"markdown","metadata":{},"source":"## Reading the eventual score honestly This version deliberately separates four kinds of evidence: 1. **Public episode evidence** identifies strategic motifs. 2. **Local route simulation** cheaply tests millions of counterfactual pairings. 3. **Exact-engine validation** checks rules fidelity on a frozen, unseen seed protocol. 4. **The completed Kaggle submission row**—and only that row—determines the official public score. The bundle above is the experiment. If it fails publicly, the failure is still informative: fixed routes can expose strong economy schedules, but a top-ten agent will almost certainly need dynamic state-aware branching around the opening and late livestock expansion. If this notebook helped you think differently about Kaggriculture, an upvote helps keep transparent strategy work visible. 🌾 "}],"metadata":{"kernelspec":{"display_name":"Python 3","language":"python","name":"python3"},"language_info":{"name":"python","version":"3.11"}},"nbformat":4,"nbformat_minor":5}
